messages:
maya (People Ops): hi folks  quick follow-up thread from the all-hands Q&A focused on parental leave, phased returns, proration for comp/bonus, and contractor->employee timing. drop Qs. office hours Fri 9-10am PT. calibration still closes Fri 11:59pm PT.

jia (SWE): can someone clarify proration for bonuses if someone is on leave during payout month?

leila (Total Rewards): short answer: bonuses are prorated by active days in the payout period unless the manager requests an exception for retention. Exceptions need Comp Exception with business rationale.

omar (Eng Manager): about phased returns  we have an IC returning 60% capacity for 3 months, do we pro-rate salary or comp? any policy?

ash (Head of People): phased returns are supported. base salary remains unchanged for first 8 weeks; after that, managers can request a temporary FTE adjustment if sustained part-time. submit a Return-to-Work plan + People Ops ticket. we avoid changing base pay retroactively unless mutually agreed.

jia (SWE): how does that affect stock vesting if someone shifts to part-time?

leila (Total Rewards): RSU schedules stay the same for up to 6 months of short-term reduced hours. for long-term part-time (>6 months) we evaluate on a case basis; legal + finance must sign off. use the Grants form for any proposed vesting changes.

maya (People Ops): note for managers: document the return plan in the Leveling/Promo packet if it affects evidence timing. we accept leave-adjusted evidence.

payroll-bot: Payroll note: for retro pay and bonus proration, allow 2 payroll cycles for US domestic, 3 for EMEA/APAC due to tax reconciliation. Submit payroll ticket ASAP with employee country.

jia (SWE): contractor->employee conversions: how soon can comp adjustments be effective and when do they get benefits?

leila (Total Rewards): benefits eligibility starts on first day of employment for converted contractors if conversion paperwork is completed before payroll cutoff. comp adjustments effective date should be the conversion date; retro pay may take 1-2 cycles.

omar (Eng Manager): appeals: IC disagrees with calibration outcome that cited reduced capacity during parental leave  what's the process?

maya (People Ops): appeals accepted within 10 business days. managers should include the Return-to-Work plan + collaborator attestations. Appeals panel looks for documented sustained scope vs temporary reduction. outcomes: uphold / revise / escalate.

jia (SWE): one last one  are there guidelines for making retention offers that include temporary top-ups during leave?

ash (Head of People): retention top-ups can be approved on a case-by-case basis. manager submits Comp Exception + Retention memo; exec sign-off likely for >15% of base. link to templates: https://redwood.internal/comp-templates and use code snippet: `forms/comp-exception?type=retention`.

leila (Total Rewards): action items: publish Parental Leave FAQ + Return-to-Work checklist by EOD Thu (Leila); Payroll to add international timeline note to KB (Payroll); People Ops to run office hours Fri 9-10am PT (Maya).

maya (People Ops): thanks  closing thread. DM or open a People Ops ticket to book 1:1 help. :heart:
